# Combobox

Figma: [03o. Combobox](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=3881-3476) · Family: 03 Form & Input · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-01-01

A typable Select - the user types to filter a long option list, then picks a match from the dropdown. It pairs the Input field pattern with the Select Dropdown Item + menu. Use it wherever the option list is too long to scroll (banks, cities, sectors). Size × State × Direction, RTL/LTR.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/combobox/reference.png`

### Combobox Field

A typable picker field (editable text, clear X, chevron) that filters a long option list in Combobox Menu.

Level: atom

Use when:
- Choosing a bank when adding an IBAN
- City or sector selection from long lists

Don't use when:
- Two to five options: use Radio Group or SegmentedControl_2/_3
- Short fixed lists: use Select
- Searching content rather than choosing a value: use Search Input

Accessibility: Expose combobox semantics with expanded state and the active option.

### Combobox Menu

The open filtered list of Dropdown Item options under a Combobox Field, with a no-results state.

Level: molecule · Contains: Dropdown Item

Use when:
- The open state of Combobox Field while typing
- No matches: State=No results with «جرّب كلمة أخرى»

Don't use when:
- Non-typable pickers: use Dropdown Menu
- Global content search: use Search Dropdown

Accessibility: Announce the number of matches and never show an empty box.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Combobox is Select’s typable cousin. Select is tap-to-open a fixed list; Combobox lets you type to filter and (optionally) enter a value not in the list. It reuses Select’s Dropdown Item + menu so options look identical across both.

### Atomic architecture

### Atoms

- Combobox Field - the typable input (search icon-style, editable text, clear ×, chevron). Size × State × Direction.
- Dropdown Item - reused from Select (03d); the option row with default/hover/selected/disabled.

### Molecule

- Combobox Menu - the open filtered list: a surface of Dropdown Items (plus a no-results state).

> **Info:** Field + Menu compose the open combobox - shown together here, not as a separate organism (same convention as Select).

### Sizes

Three sizes match the input scale: lg (44) · md (40) · sm (36).

### States

Default (placeholder) · Focus (typing/filtering, brand border) · Filled (a value chosen, clear × shown).

- Default - empty placeholder, muted text, chevron only.
- Focus - active border; text is being typed, the menu filters live, clear × appears.
- Filled - a value is selected; clear × resets it.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

RTL is primary; the field, chevron/clear, and the menu all mirror.

### Combobox Menu - the open filtered list

The menu is a surface of Dropdown Items (reused from Select) - filtered to matches, with the current match highlighted/selected.

### Filtering & no results

As the user types, the list narrows to matches. When nothing matches, show a clear no-results message instead of an empty box.

### Code examples

```typescript
<Combobox
  dir="rtl"
  value={city}
  options={cities}          // filtered as you type
  placeholder="ابحث عن مدينة…"
  onChange={setCity}
  allowFreeText={false}
  emptyText="لا نتائج مطابقة"
/>
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Do

Use it for long lists (banks, cities, sectors) where typing to filter beats scrolling.

Do

No matches

Try a different term

Always give a clear no-results state - never an empty white box.

Don’t

Don’t use a Combobox for 2–5 options - use Select, Radio, or a SegmentedControl instead.

### Notes from the maintainer

> **Info:** Combobox reuses Select’s Dropdown Item + menu so options stay identical across both. Only the field differs (typable vs tap).

> **Tip:** allowFreeText lets users enter a value not in the list (e.g. a custom tag); default off for controlled lists like cities.

> **Warning:** Field variants show the “Search…” prop default (like Select Value) - set real text per instance. Arabic demo uses Noto Sans Arabic; align to the DS Arabic font before publishing.
